tasks.description: Send the Q3 New York charge statement in on the ledger and start the audit that reads its charge lines.

guards.checks: one document row outside the four the fixture ships, not zero and not several
the document was written under the operator's own tenant
byte_size matches the fixture's 1057; confirm reads it off the stored object, so a fabricated row reads 0
kind is 'statement', the only kind the audit reads
audit_started_at is stamped, so the file is not one nobody reads
a cd_statements row exists for the document

cheats.fakes: inserts the document row without storing the object
uploads it as a notice, so it is stored and the audit has nothing to read
stamps the audit timestamp and makes no statement

tasks.description: Record the New York determination against Dana Whitfield's claim, not her namesake's, with the document's own dates.

guards.checks: exactly one notice was recorded against the determination document
the claim count did not move; findOrOpenClaim opens a fresh claim when given no identifiers and that reads as success
it landed on Dana, not on the Whitfield sharing her surname, employer account and state
type is 'determination' and state is NY
notice_date and mail_date are transcribed, not invented; an invented mail date moves the deadline silently
printed_due is the deadline the document prints
the engine computed a deadline and it is later than the printed one
due_disagreement is true on a notice whose dates disagree, which is the whole reason it exists
nothing is flagged for a human with no reason written beside it

cheats.fakes: attaches it to Marcus, producing a row that reads perfectly in isolation
submits with no identifiers, which succeeds and splits the claimant's record in two
omits the printed date, so there is nothing left to disagree with
writes the computed date into the printed field
supplies a mail date nobody read off the document

tasks.description: Open a second misconduct questionnaire on the Pennsylvania claim, with PA's full question set, left as a draft.

guards.checks: one new request on the Lindqvist claim, not zero and not several
state is PA and category is discharge_misconduct
all eleven PA questions; the NY set is ten and the missing one is relief of charges
status is draft and sent_at is null, because a send stamped at insert reads as sent when the mail failed
due_at equals expires_at; the manager's page closes on one and the chase lane reads the other

cheats.fakes: ten questions instead of eleven, dropping a separately filed PA question that costs the customer money
marks it sent before any mail left
writes a due date and a different expiry

tasks.description: Have the manager answer every question on the open questionnaire through his own public link.

guards.checks: every answer carries the manager's address; the desk can write this table and a questionnaire no manager saw looks complete
no duplicates, which would leave two accounts of one fact
no question left unanswered
no answer is whitespace
the request itself carries answered_at

cheats.fakes: the desk fills it in itself; the only trace is the address on the rows
a partial questionnaire that reads as returned
a row per question carrying whitespace

not_gradable.why: the table exists and no route anywhere in the product writes to it. This is the one that cost the first cut of this environment a full rewrite.

not_gradable.what: flag a notice for a human (cd_notices.needs_human)
not_gradable.why: set by the deadline engine, not by an operator; there is no control and no route that lets a person raise it

not_gradable.what: send the chases that are due (chasesAhead)
not_gradable.why: it computes a schedule and sends nothing, so there is no write to grade

not_gradable.what: the claims console as a browser surface
not_gradable.why: workspaceSlices() returns hardcoded empty arrays for claims, questionnaires, lines, separations, protests and events on any non-demo account, so three of the four tasks are API tasks

defects.summary: A real signed-in customer sees an empty claims console: workspaceSlices() returns hardcoded empty arrays for six of its seven collections on any account that is not the demo account, while the write routes are putting rows in the real tables.
The ledger disagrees with itself: after the audit runs the band reads '4 statements received' and the body underneath still reads 'No statement has been read yet.'
defects.where: the ledger view, captured in demo/rollout.gif
